questions.prompt: Cards are in the air and it is not your turn. You should…

choices.text: Wait. Acting out of turn creates confusion and can bind you.
Fold out of turn to speed the game up.
Announce 'raise' before the player on your right.
Show one card so the table can help.

questions.explanation: Act in turn. Early declarations can be binding or angle-adjacent.

questions.prompt: Your neighbor bets and you have not looked yet. Best action?

choices.text: Call while still looking at your cards.
Look first, then act in turn when action reaches you.
Ask the dealer to pause the hand until you choose a seat.

questions.explanation: Protect the order of action. Look before it is your turn, then act once.

questions.prompt: A player asks what you folded. A clean answer is…

choices.text: Tell them the exact two cards every time.
Show the fold to the whole table.
Decline. Folded cards stay hidden unless a rule requires otherwise.
Write the hand on a phone in the middle of the hand.

questions.explanation: You do not owe folded-hand information. Phones at the table are often restricted.

choices.text: Win the most pots, even by guessing.
Stack off light to 'see where you are'.
Straddle every hand so you look active.
Avoid big mistakes while you learn the table.

questions.explanation: Survival and information beat heroics on a brand-new table.
